1.explanation:
All of the logic that drives the page-size dropdown and the subsequent range/page calculations lives inside the Pagination class.  
• In propTypes the component only accepts an array of numbers (`pageSizes: PropTypes.arrayOf(PropTypes.number)`), so passing objects breaks type assumptions.  
• In render(), it maps each `size` in pageSizes to a <SelectItem key={size} value={size} text={String(size)} />; custom objects aren’t handled and String(size) yields '[object Object]'.  
• handleSizeChange immediately does `Number(evt.target.value)`, which also yields NaN for a non-numeric value.  
• renderSelectItems and the math in render() (computing totalPages and itemRangeText) all rely on numeric pageSize values.  
To fix this, Pagination.render (mapping logic), handleSizeChange (value parsing), renderSelectItems (if used for custom labels), and the propTypes declaration on Pagination must be updated to accept and correctly handle objects of shape {value, text} as well as plain numbers.
1.bug_scenario: In the Pagination component, a developer wants to supply a custom “All” option alongside numeric page sizes so that selecting “All” displays all items at once. They passed an array of objects like `{value: totalItems, text: 'All'}`, but because the component only expects numbers, the dropdown still shows “All” (the label is coerced from the object) but all of the other count labels in the pagination (item ranges and page totals) become NaN–NaN, “of NaN pages”, etc.

2.explanation:
All of the key logic for page size handling lives in the `Pagination` class of `Pagination.js`. 

• constructor(props): Initializes state.pageSize by checking membership against the numeric `pageSizes` array. Because custom objects won’t match by `includes()`, custom values break this logic. 

• static propTypes: Currently enforces `pageSizes` as `arrayOf(PropTypes.number)`. To support custom labels, this must be widened (e.g. to allow objects with `{value, text}`). 

• handleSizeChange(evt): Casts `evt.target.value` to a Number unconditionally, which turns object stringifications into `NaN`. 

• render(): Maps `pageSizes.map(size => <SelectItem value={size} text={String(size)} />)`. This assumes each entry is a number and uses it directly for both value and display text. To support separate `value` and `text`, this mapping must be updated to detect object entries and extract `.value` and `.text` fields instead of treating every entry as a raw number.
2.bug_scenario: The Pagination component only accepts an array of numbers for its `pageSizes` prop and uses each numeric size both as the option’s value and its displayed text. When a developer instead passes an array of objects (e.g. `{ value: totalItems, text: 'All' }`), the `<SelectItem>` ends up stringifying the object as its value (`"[object Object]"`). Calling `Number(evt.target.value)` then yields `NaN`, which propagates through the state and renders labels like "NaN–NaN of 200 items" and "of NaN pages".
